transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I came in because I can’t stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Like at work, if something gets delayed, even if it’s not really on me, I still feel like I’m a bad employee. And then at home too—like with the house, there’s always something, you know, repairs or bills, and I start thinking I’m a bad homeowner and maybe I don’t deserve to keep any of it.

Sorry, I know that’s kind of a lot. It’s just been sitting on me all the time.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, when I look back on it, it’s not like it comes and goes in a normal way. The sadness has been there almost the whole time since this started, and I don’t really get interested in things the way I used to.

There are little stretches where I can kind of function better, like get through work or keep up with stuff around the house, but it doesn’t last very long. Then it’s just… back to that heavy feeling again.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been… a little over two years, I think. About two years and one month.

I remember trying to pin it down because there was a work project around then, and I kept thinking I was just tired from that, but then it didn’t lift. And I kept telling myself after the next thing was done I’d feel normal again, but… the sadness and not really caring about things stayed.
Do you find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy before you started feeling this way?

Not really, no. I mean… I used to be the person who planned brunches with friends, and I’d paint in the spare room, and I liked hiking when the weather was decent. I even used to sign up for networking events, which sounds boring, but I actually kind of enjoyed meeting people.

Now all of that feels like… chores, almost. Like I’m pretending to care because I remember that I used to care. Even if I go, I’m mostly just getting through it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight since you started feeling this way?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t weigh myself a lot, so I can’t give you an exact number, but my clothes have definitely been looser.

My appetite’s been kind of all over the place. Most days I don’t really eat proper meals during the day, and then I’ll realize I’ve basically had coffee, maybe toast, and then whatever’s easiest later. Like, I’ll stand in the kitchen and just not want to deal with making anything. It’s weird because I used to meal prep sometimes—well, not perfectly, but I had containers and everything—and now I just sort of… forget, or avoid it, and then suddenly my jeans don’t fit the same.
Have you had periods in your life where you felt completely better from these feelings of sadness and lack of interest, only to have them return later?

Um… not really completely better, no. Like, there have been stretches where I could kind of keep up more—go to work, answer texts, do the normal things without it feeling quite as impossible.

But looking back, the sadness and the not-caring feeling have pretty much been there almost the whole time since it started. It’s more like the volume changes, if that makes sense. Sometimes it’s quieter and I can function better for a bit, but I don’t think it ever fully went away and then came back fresh.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt completely back to your normal self?

No… I don’t think I’ve had two whole months where I felt totally like myself again. I mean, there were little stretches where I could sort of keep up better—like I’d answer emails on time or make plans and actually show up—but the low mood and the not really enjoying things was still kind of there underneath.

It’s like… some weeks I could pass better as normal, if that makes sense, but looking back it never fully lifted for that long.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that others couldn't hear or see?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if “seen things” exactly, but I’ve heard a voice sometimes. It’s usually like a woman’s voice, and it sounds like it’s coming from the hallway, or once I thought it was through the air vent, which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud.

She’ll say things like, “You’re going to lose it all.” And it feels so real in the moment that I’ve actually gone outside to check who was there. Like, I’ll be standing there in my socks by the door, and then I’m thinking about how the neighbors probably think I’m strange because I’m always trying to look normal when I run into them by the mailboxes… sorry, that’s not really the point. But yes, I’ve heard that.
How often do you hear the voice?

It’s not constant… I wouldn’t say I hear it all day or anything. It happens sometimes, usually when I’m at home, and it’ll sound like a woman in the hallway or through the air vent saying something like, “You’re going to lose it all.”

And then I get stuck on it because it sounds so real, like I’ll actually go check outside to see if someone was there. Which is embarrassing, because then I start thinking about who saw me doing that, and the neighbors already kind of look at me funny sometimes—sorry. But, yeah… not every day, exactly, just often enough that I don’t really feel like I can ignore it.
Do you hear the voice even when you're feeling a little better and able to function more normally?

Yeah… yes, I think so. There was a stretch of a few weeks where my mood wasn’t as heavy, like I was getting through work more normally and answering things and not falling behind as much.

But even then I still heard the voice near the vents. And I was still pretty sure the mortgage company was watching me somehow, and that my coworkers were monitoring what I was doing. I know that sounds… I don’t know. I was functioning better, but that part didn’t really go away.
Did the voice and the feelings of being watched go away when you were feeling a little better?

No, not really. I mean, my mood got a little lighter for a few weeks—like I was getting through work more normally, keeping up with emails and tasks better—but the voice didn’t exactly stop.

I still heard it near the vents, and I still felt pretty sure the mortgage company was watching me somehow. And at work, I kept thinking my coworkers were monitoring what I was doing. Even when I was functioning better, that part was still there.
Did you ever have a period where you didn't hear the voice for at least two weeks when your mood was lighter?

No… I don’t think so. There was that stretch of several weeks where I wasn’t as weighed down and I was getting through work more normally—like keeping up with things better, not just staring at my inbox forever—but I still heard the voice near the vents.

And I still had that feeling that the mortgage company was watching me, and at work I kept thinking my coworkers were monitoring what I was doing. So… even when my mood was lighter, I don’t think there was a full two weeks where it all stopped.
Have you ever had a time when you heard the voice and it told you something positive?

Positive? No… not really. It’s usually more like a woman’s voice, like from the hallway or the air vent, saying things like, “You’re going to lose it all.”

And it sounds real enough that I’ve actually gone outside to check who was there, which is embarrassing because then there’s nobody. I mean, sometimes vents make weird noises anyway—my apartment does that when the heat kicks on—but this feels like words, not just noise. So… no, I wouldn’t say it’s ever been positive.
Did the voice you hear go away when you were not feeling sad or down?

No, it didn’t really go away. There was a stretch for a few weeks where I wasn’t feeling as heavy, like I could get through work more normally, and I wasn’t just dragging through everything.

But I still heard the voice near the vents. And I still felt like the mortgage company was watching me somehow, and at work I kept thinking my coworkers were monitoring me. I know that sounds… I don’t know. But even when I wasn’t as sad, that was still happening.
Did the voice only happen when you were feeling sad or down?

No, not only then. I mean, I wish it worked that way, like it was just when I was really low and then it would lift with everything else, but… there was a stretch of several weeks where my mood wasn’t as heavy. I was getting through work more normally, answering things, keeping up better.

And it still happened. I still heard the voice near the vents. I’d be trying to focus and then I’d hear it, and then I’d start thinking about the vents in my apartment too, because they make noises sometimes, but this was different. And I was still pretty convinced the mortgage company was watching me somehow, and at work I felt like my coworkers were monitoring what I was doing.

So… no, it wasn’t just when I was sad or down.
Did the voice or the feeling of being watched only happen when you were feeling sad or down?

No, it wasn’t only when I was sad. I mean, there was that stretch for several weeks where I wasn’t feeling so weighed down, and I was getting through work more normally—like doing my tasks, answering emails, all that normal stuff.

But the voice was still there near the vents. And I still had that feeling, or… more like I was convinced, that the mortgage company was watching me somehow, and that my coworkers were monitoring what I was doing. So it didn’t really match up just with feeling down.
Did you only hear the voice when you were feeling sad or down?

No… not only then. I know I keep circling back to this, but there were a few weeks where I wasn’t feeling as heavy, like I could actually get through work more normally and not feel completely stuck.

And even during that time, I still heard the voice near the vents. The vents are weird anyway, they make noises, and I always notice that kind of thing in buildings, like at work too with the air system… but this was still happening. And I still felt sure the mortgage company was watching me somehow, and that my coworkers were monitoring me. So it wasn’t just when I was sad or down.
Do the voice and feelings of being watched only occur when you're feeling sad or down, or do they happen at other times as well?

They happen at other times too. There was, um… a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn’t as down, like I could get through work more normally and keep up with things.

But even then I still heard the voice near the vents. And I was still convinced the mortgage company was watching me somehow, and that people at work were monitoring what I was doing. It’s hard to explain because vents already make noises, you know, so I’d start thinking about that, but… no, it wasn’t only when I was sad.
Do the voice and feelings of being watched only happen when you're feeling your worst, or can they also occur when your mood is not as low?

It can happen when my mood isn’t as low too. Like I said, there was that stretch for several weeks where I wasn’t feeling quite so heavy, and I was getting through work more normally.

I mean, work has all these little routines and emails and people walking by, and sometimes I can sort of function through it, but even then I still heard the voice near the vents. And I still felt really sure the mortgage company was watching me somehow, and that my coworkers were monitoring what I was doing. So… no, it’s not only when I’m at my worst.
Has there ever been a time when you didn't hear the voice for at least a month?

I don’t think so… not a whole month. It’s hard to measure because sometimes I try to ignore it, and then I’ll hear something in the hallway or through the air vent and I’m right back checking.

It’s usually a woman’s voice, and it says things like, “You’re going to lose it all.” It sounds real enough that I’ve gone outside to see if someone was actually there. I know vents carry weird sounds, like in offices and apartments, but… no, I can’t really think of a full month where it just didn’t happen.
